title: Dojo definition (dojos/<id>.json)
description: A practice room for one procedure. Pure data: add a file and list its id in pack.json to get a new dojo, no code needed.

procedure.description: The algorithm or method, e.g. 'Powerset construction NFA → DFA'.

chapter.description: Id of a chapter of the subject, for dojos that belong to one part of it.

topics.description: Topic ids in the subject that this dojo trains.

aids.description: Tools to use or assume, e.g. a specific calculator.

answerFormat.description: How the learner should write the answer, e.g. a transition table.

symbols.description: Formula symbols offered as buttons while answering, e.g. ["σ", "⋈"], or group names: automata, sets, numbers, logic, relational-algebra, compare, calculus, powers, arrows, greek, brackets. The app also adds symbols it finds in the task and the answer key.

drills.description: Prepared exercises that run in the app as a timed practice round and are graded without an AI.

transitions.description: [from, symbol, to]. Use "ε" as the symbol for ε-transitions.

reference.description: The correct language, as a regular expression or an automaton. Answers are correct when they describe the same language.

regex.description: Single-character symbols, | union, * + ? postfix, parentheses, ε for the empty word, ∅ for the empty language.

prompt.description: The question or task (Markdown; an ```automaton block is drawn as a state diagram).

explanation.description: Shown after answering: why the answer is right (Markdown).

seconds.description: Time limit. Default: 60/120/240 s for easy/medium/exam, doubled for automaton, regex and self.

correct.description: Indexes into options (0-based). Several = pick all of them.

accept.description: Accepted answers. Compared without case, extra spaces or spaces around punctuation.

items.description: In the correct order; the app shuffles them.

given.description: An automaton shown with the task, e.g. the NFA to convert.

minimal.description: Answer must have as few states as the minimal complete DFA.

given.description: An automaton shown with the task, e.g. the DFA to turn into a regex.

solution.description: Model solution the learner compares with (Markdown).
